name: Take Input
html:
Welcome back, dear reader. So, today we are going to learn about Take Input.


Important Links :Introduction Video

Why is taking input necessary?

Every time we write a programming, we cannot change the contents of our code to accommodate various changing parameters which may depend upon user input.

For example: If a user inputs his name for output, we would have to write his name for him in the output by ourselves (This is also known as hard-coding) instead of the machine working for us.

To overcome this problem, we use variables and the method of taking input value directly from user using a keyboard and storing this value in a variable and then further, performing operations on variables accordingly.

Basic Programming Tools:

There are 5 basic tools for programming:

  1. Console Output ( Display on monitor)
  2. Variable declaration (and Initialization)
  3. Conditional Statements ( If-else-then)
  4. Creating loops ( for, while , do-while)
  5. Console Input ( Taking input from keyboard)

We will discuss the 5th point in detail and also how to take input in the Java programming language.

import java.util.*; public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); //This lines helps take input from keyboard int i = scn.nextInt(); //This line stores that input(integer) inside a integer variable } }
java; true";

The above illustration shows how to take an integer value as input from keyboard and store it inside an integer variable.

The line Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in) can be broken down

Following this, we store the integer input value provided by user in an integer variable "i".

We construct a for loop for the purpose of displaying counting up to the integer value given input.

import java.util.*; public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int i = scn.nextInt(); for(int j =0 ; j<=i;j++) { System.out.println(j); } } }
java; true";

This produces the output on given an input value of "5":

Moving forward, we can also taking strings from the user in input and store them in string variables in the following way:

import java.util.*; public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); String name = scn.nextLine(); System.out.println("Hello" + name); } }
java; true";

The above code produces the output on being given the input value Pepcoders:

While taking integers and string values separately is very easy and simple, there is a slight complication which we might encounter while taking them together from the user simultaneously.

import java.util.*; public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int i = scn.nextInt(); String name = scn.nextLine(); System.out.println("Hello" + name); System.out.println("Here is the counting:"); for(int j=0;j<=i;j++) { System.out.println(j); } } }
java; true";

The above code will produce the output as: (given input being 5 and Pepcoders)

Whereas the desired output was

To overcome this issue of not being able to output the string that we give as input along with the counting, while taking integer input, we write make slight changes to the code:

import java.util.*; public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int i = Integer.parseInt(scn.nextInt()); String name = scn.nextLine(); System.out.println("Hello" + name); System.out.println("Here is the counting:"); for(int j=0;j<=i;j++) { System.out.println(j); } } }
java; true";

This change in the way of taking an integer input is to be done only when taking both string and integer inputs simultaneously, and gives us the correct desired output.

The reason why this happens is that the "nextInt()" method does not read the newline character of our input, so when the "nextLine()" command is issued, the scanner object finds the new line character and gives you that as output.

So here, what we see is actually the newline character being stored inside the string variable and being output as is. But that issue is resolved when we use Integer.parseInt() function because this function reads the input as a string including the newline character and then returns to the variable an integer value, resolving the issue of input.


So, dear reader, we hope that you have understood the complete topic. If you still have any doubts, we recommend you refer to the Introduction Video to clear them.
